result.instructions: The user's long-term memory of past sessions, all projects; each tool's description says when and how to use it. Search before a factual question, a recommendation or a new task. When memories were shown to you this turn, call `memory_credit` once you know what you used, before your final message: the ids that informed it (it returns the line to print), or `verdict: none`. An empty search: one line «> 🧠🔍 **Nothing in memory** — <topic>». Store decisions, corrections, conventions, pitfalls and lessons with `memory_store`. User-wide rules override conflicting project facts.

tools.description: Declare the memories shown in this session that informed your answer; a search sent in the same message must return its result first. Verdict `used` (the default) returns the line to print in your final message. Use verdict confirmed only for a memory whose fact this session established independently of it (the user's words, a file, a command output): it did not inform the answer, and you checked it here. Never as a default, never for a memory you did not check; it takes no evidence and returns its own line to print. Use verdict wrong when this session shows the memory is false, outdated when it was true but no longer is; give the right fact as correction and what in this session shows it as evidence (the user's words, a file, a command output). When verdicts differ, make one call per verdict. Example: {"ids": ["7e1f9d03"], "verdict": "wrong", "correction": "Billing runs PostgreSQL 16, not 15.", "evidence": "psql --version printed 16.4"}.

ids.description: 1-10 memory ids, full or their first 8 characters; none with verdict none

verdict.description: used (default), confirmed, none, wrong or outdated

correction.description: with wrong or outdated: 1-3 sentences, as for memory_store

evidence.description: with wrong or outdated: at most 300 characters

tools.name: memory_credit

tools.description: Read one memory by id: its text, dates, project and the source facts (with their kinds and documents) it was built from.

id.description: the memory id shown by memory_search, or the short id (first 8 characters) of a memory shown in this session

tools.name: memory_read

tools.description: Search the user's long-term memory: what was discussed, decided and learned in past sessions across all projects (decisions and their reasons, conventions, infrastructure facts, project history, mistakes already made). Use it BEFORE asking the user a factual question or a preference, recommending an architecture, tool or convention, starting a task or topic, writing a test or changing something shared, or when the user refers to the past. Skip it for trivial edits and a fact already found this session. Queries: one per angle, topic + intent word ("docker compose subnet pitfall"), never a kind word alone nor a copy of the user's sentence; add a date or version for a question about time. Before a risky or irreversible action search topic + pitfall / correction; before design work topic + decision; before asking a preference topic + convention / correction. The task involves another project (shared code, infrastructure, a decision made there): name it in `projects`. Hits show their kinds [pitfall, state]. Results are hints from past sessions: verify them against the code.

projects.description: other projects to search fully, exact names as listed at session start; unnamed, a project is reached only by a strong match

scope.description: auto (current project, transverse, related projects and the whole memory; default) or all (the whole memory only)

min_score.description: relevance floor (default 0.4); lower it to widen

tools.name: memory_search

tools.description: Store one durable fact per call (split a fact that covers two topics), exact identifiers; no code dumps, no secrets, no plans or hypotheses, no merges, releases or CI status (the conversation has them), a delivered state only with a reason or location the conversation lacks; state the fact itself, never "a memory about X was stored". Example: "Decision (2026-10-24): billing keeps PostgreSQL 16 because partial indexes are required." Close the loop: when a recalled open item is settled (shipped, abandoned, root cause found) or a recalled memory is contradicted by the code or the user, store ONE dated fact that names the old claim in its own words ("State (2026-10-27): <item> is <status>; replaces open item <old wording>"); kind correction for a contradiction. Print the line the result gives: Updated if the fact updates the memory it shows (no parallel fact), else Saved; a repeat: say so in it.

kind.description: decision, correction, convention, pitfall, state or lesson

text.description: 1-3 sentences: the fact, why, absolute dates (2026-10-24, never "today")

project.description: default: the current project; "transverse" only for a user-wide rule (it reaches every project)

tools.name: memory_store
